name: Levaillant's Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: A large, dark-backed cuckoo with a floppy crest, white wing patches, and pale underparts; throat and lower flanks both heavily streaked. It is a brood parasite on babblers and other medium-sized birds.

name: Tawny-collared Nightjar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern mexico (nuevo león to oaxaca and chiapas)
description: Fairly large dark nightjar of woodland, edge, and adjacent clearings in northeast Mexico. Hunts mainly from perches at forest edge, sometimes even on fence posts in rather open areas.

name: Abyssinian Roller
rangeDescription: Senegambia to ethiopia, somalia, and kenya; central arabia
description: A slim and beautiful roller with very long outer tail feathers. In flight, the spectacular wings are half pale blue and half dark blue.

name: Scrub Nightjar
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Brown-and-buff nightbird found in arid scrub and deserts in western Ecuador and northwestern Peru. It is dark brown, heavily mottled with buff, and has a white throat.

name: Sumba Brown Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Sumba (lesser sundas)
description: An unremarkable drab, brown flycatcher, gray-brown above and pale below. Note the pale base to the bill.

name: Black-thighed Puffleg
rangeDescription: Central andes of colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Scintillating hummingbird of the high Andes of Colombia and far northern Ecuador (it does not reach the Quito area). Male is dark glittering-green (with brighter rump and vent) and has inconspicuous black leg puffs.

name: White-bearded Antshrike
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southeastern minas gerais) to far northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Unmistakable medium-sized antshrike, with a long tail and a short bill. Inhabits the understory of dense humid forest and second growth with bamboo.

name: Yellow-breasted Pipit
rangeDescription: Eastern south africa (mpumalanga southward to northeastern eastern cape) and lesotho
description: A medium-sized scaly-backed pipit. In breeding plumage, it is easily told by its canary yellow throat and breast.

name: Streaky-breasted Flufftail
rangeDescription: Locally in wet grassland of central africa
description: Small rail of grassland habitats. Very shy and elusive bird that is unlikely to be seen unless expressly searched for.

name: Socorro Dove
rangeDescription: Formerly socorro island (off western mexico); extinct in the wild since 1950s but a small captive population exists
description: Slender dove native to Socorro Island, located in the Pacific Ocean 360 miles from mainland Mexico. It was wiped out due to introduced feral cats and habitat loss, and last seen there in the seventies.

name: Gola Malimbe
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone, liberia, and southwestern ivory coast
description: A striking black-and-yellow malimbe; the female lacks the yellow nape of the male. Juvenile has a pale bill and yellow on the crown and chin.

name: Elfin Myzomela
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed mountains of new guinea
description: A tiny honeyeater of mid-montane forest canopy and villages. Brown with a whitish belly and fairly short curved bill.

name: Reischek's Parakeet
rangeDescription: Antipodes islands
description: A medium-sized, emerald-green parakeet endemic to the Antipodes Islands, including smaller outer islands. Recognized by its distinctive bright red crown and small red patches behind the eyes.

name: Scaled Pigeon
rangeDescription: Tropical southern mexico to brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Handsome large pigeon of humid forest and edge in tropical lowlands. Usually seen flying overhead, less often perched in canopy of tall trees.

name: Javan Woodcock
rangeDescription: Mountains of sumatra and western java
description: Rare and reclusive long-billed inhabitant of moist montane and foothill forests at 1350-3000 meters. Dark brown and heavily patterned overall, with densest patterning on the back.

name: Eastern Wattled-Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Eastern fiji, lau archipelago, tonga, and samoa
description: A medium-sized, grayish-olive honeyeater with an olive cast to the throat, back, and wings. Note the large bright yellow wattle from bill base to neck.

name: Far Eastern Curlew
rangeDescription: Breeds northeastern asia; winters to philippines, indonesia, and australia
description: This very large curlew wields a remarkable scimitar-like bill, used to extract invertebrates from deep burrows. Typically found in small to mid-sized groups on expansive mudflats.

name: Small-billed Elaenia
rangeDescription: Southern brazil to bolivia and central argentina; winters north to colombia
description: A fairly small and very dull-looking flycatcher. Grayish brown above and whitish below with a thin white eyering, three pale wingbars, and pinkish base to the bill.

name: Henderson Island Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Henderson island (pitcairn archipelago)
description: A large warbler with a variably white head and body. Crown and uppersides often mottled olive-brown and white, underside often tinted yellow.

name: White-bellied Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of peru (huánuco) to western bolivia (santa cruz)
description: A tiny puffball of feathers that looks like a bumblebee crossed with a down pillow. Minute size and compact shape prevent confusion with most other species, but also note the faint dusky streaking on whitish underparts, indistinct black crescent behind the eye, and olive-yellow upperparts.
